title: Explain a version with a release
summary: A Git tag names a specific point in history. A GitHub release can add notes and downloadable files around a tag.
introduction: A Git tag names a specific point in history. A GitHub release can add notes and downloadable files around a tag. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain explain a version with a release
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A Git tag names a specific point in history. A GitHub release can add notes and downloadable files around a tag.

blocks.code:
Tag: v1.1.0
Release title: Search improvement
Notes: search now ignores letter case
Known limit: outside spaces are still significant
blocks.title: Explain a version with a release

blocks.text: The notes tell users what changed and what still matters. Later commits are not automatically part of the tagged version.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Write a release note for handling outside spaces in search.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not claim a release fixes all bugs when only one behaviour changed.
For more detail later, use this [GitHub further reading](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started).
